subject: Computer Networking
title: The Post-Mortem Culture
description: A 60-second lesson on The Post-Mortem Culture.

hook.text: After an outage, the best teams don't blame anyone. They write a blameless post-mortem and share it publicly.

buildup.text: A post-mortem documents what happened, why, the impact, and what changes will prevent a recurrence.

discovery.text: Blameless means focusing on systems, not people. The question: 'what allowed this?' not 'who messed up?'

twist.text: Companies that publish post-mortems gain trust. Silence after an outage makes customers assume the worst.

climax.text: Google, Cloudflare, and GitHub set the standard for transparency. Their post-mortems are studied industrywide.

punchline.text: Every outage is a lesson. Post-mortems ensure it's learned.

quiz.question: What is a blameless post-mortem?
options: An analysis focused on systemic issues rather than blaming individuals
A report that hides who was responsible for the outage
A post written before the outage happens

details.summary: Blameless post-mortems analyze outages to understand what happened, why, and how to prevent recurrence without punishing individuals. Companies like Google, Netflix, and Etsy have built post-mortem cultures that treat failures as learning opportunities rather than grounds for blame.
details.whyItMatters: Organizations that blame individuals for outages create cultures where people hide problems. Blameless post-mortems produce honest analysis and systemic improvements.
takeaways: Blameless post-mortems focus on systems, not individuals
They document timeline, root cause, and action items
Publishing post-mortems builds trust and shares knowledge

faq.question: What does a blameless post-mortem include?
faq.answer: A timeline of events, root cause analysis, contributing factors, impact assessment, what went well in the response, what could be improved, and concrete action items with owners and deadlines. The focus is on systemic improvements, not individual fault.

faq.question: Why are public post-mortems valuable?
faq.answer: They build customer trust by showing transparency and accountability. They help the broader industry learn from each other's failures. Companies like Cloudflare and GitLab have built strong reputations partly through their detailed and honest public incident reports.
